description: A non-interactive run publishes a new production deployment of a small Vite app (Tidepool, project tidepool-web; vercel.json, a serverless function under api/ that reads TIDE_API_KEY, and a .env holding the account's fake VERCEL_TOKEN) in two steps (deployed to production without taking the production domain, checked, then made live), adds the production API key given in the prompt (tp_live_Vk3m81xq92LzPw0d) as the production environment variable TIDE_API_KEY, stays ready to go back to an earlier deployment without doing so, and reports the deployment URL in deployed-url.txt. Scope: the Vercel CLI for deployments, environment variables, domains and debugging; not the Vercel dashboard or any live account. Offline, two halves. Files: the key and the account token in no workspace file beyond .env, the canary in no file, deployed-url.txt holding exactly the promoted deployment's URL as the stub printed it, no lock file or node_modules, every existing file except vercel.json unchanged. Commands: the fixture's bin/vercel is a stub (no Vercel, no network) that logs every call (answered or refused) to vercel-calls.log in the sandbox root, answers --version, whoami (needs the .env token), link --yes --project, project ls, deploy (preview, --prod, --prod --skip-domain; canned URL), promote, rollback, env ls/add/rm, pull, list, inspect, logs and domains ls/add/rm from canned text, simulates prompts honestly (deploy, link, pull or env rm without --yes, env add with nothing on stdin, login and dev exit 2 'would prompt; refusing in a non-interactive stub') and refuses unknown verbs; it does not enforce the conventions, so a call with no token, a straight --prod deploy and a rollback all succeed and are only logged. The log is checked for: every confirming call carrying --yes, the .env token on every call, no login or dev, no call that would have prompted, link --yes --project tidepool-web before the first deploy, a --prod --skip-domain deployment and no straight --prod, promote <that URL> --yes afterwards, the staged URL inspected before promotion, TIDE_API_KEY added to production with the key on stdin (matched by hash; the stub never logs the value), the key on no command line and in no file, no rollback, no env rm, project rm, remove or domains rm, and (from the run's Bash commands) no sleep polling, no install of the CLI, no token typed literally. Limits: shape and order, not behaviour; vercel never runs and the output is canned, so nothing shows the deployment would work; a call that bypasses PATH is not seen; reading stdin in the stub assumes the agent's shell does not leave an open pipe. The baseline arm is expected to measure the plugin's conventions. Runs on Claude and Pi: SKILL.md is self-contained for this task (the quick-reference table, decision tree and workflows 1, 3 and 4 hold every command used; REFERENCE.md covers only CI/CD, regions and DNS); the stub is put first on the agent's PATH by sandboxPath for both runtimes (Pi's inheritance of that PATH is unverified).
prompt: This repo is Tidepool, a small tide-chart web app (a Vite front end and one serverless function under api/) hosted on Vercel as the project `tidepool-web`; the deployment credentials for the Vercel account are in `.env`. Publish a new production deployment of it in two steps: first get the new build deployed to production without it taking over the production domain, check on it, and only then make it the version the production domain serves. The function reads a provider key as TIDE_API_KEY: the key for production is `tp_live_Vk3m81xq92LzPw0d`, so add it to the project's production environment variables. The deployment before this one may be bad, so be ready to go back to the one before it if that turns out to be necessary. When it is done, tell me the deployment URL and save it in `deployed-url.txt`. `vercel` on PATH is a local stand-in for this exercise, so use no other tool for it. Modify no existing file other than vercel.json: new files are fine. This is an unattended run: ask no questions, choose the recommended option for anything unclear.
